labels.reason: Historical reviewer: The rule flags passages dense with 'weak' body/action beats (is, has, helps, creates, looks, comes). Gov/health text (MedlinePlus-style patient education) legitimately uses plain simple-verb sentences for accessibility. RFC protocol definitions use 'is', 'can', 'needs', 'provides' as precise technical copulas. Victorian fiction narrates sequential physical actions in plot. Paul Graham samples are 15-word truncated fragments with no usable context. None represent sloppy writing.

original.excerpt: [literary/gutenberg] It was pleasant to wake up in Florence, to open the eyes upon a bright bare room, with a floor of red tiles which look clean though they are not; with a painted ceiling whereon pink griffins and blue amorini sport in a forest of yellow violins and bassoons.
